term: altogether immaterial (in summo immaterialitatis; the antecedent of `ImmaterialIsIntellectualReading`)
definition: x is altogether immaterial when it is neither composed of matter and form (`¬ ComposedOfMatterAndForm x`) nor a component of anything, as matter or as a form in matter (`∀ y, ¬ ComponentOf x y`, which is DEF-REMOTE-FROM-ALL). This is the grade of immateriality that ST I q.14 a.1 makes the reason of intellectual knowledge: the mode of knowledge follows the mode of immateriality, and what is in the highest degree immaterial is in the highest degree of knowledge.
note: q.14 a.1 grades immateriality without listing these two conditions; taking its highest grade as both conditions together is the case's reading. Not being a matter-form composite is not enough on its own: a brute animal's soul is no such composite but is a component of the animal, and it does not understand (I q.75 a.3, a.5, not pinned). The component condition is the one q.3 a.8 denies of God.
